title: Exactly what I want
body:
Personal Reason for Having App:

First off I bought both the workout and the nutrition apps of the subscription, and rarely do I hop on subscription.  I’ve been trying to keep track of both my own workout and nutrition from google spread sheets and over time it’s become more work to try and do everything on your own.  As I’ve gotten to use it for a couple of weeks now, I can say that it is much simpler, and a lot easier to track all the important details without you needing to do any extra thinking.

Both MacroFactor Workouts & Nutrition:

For the workout side, it was convenient for me to tell the app what is available for me for equipment and also what parts I’m trying to target, and when logging in my weights, it even adjusted a suggested weight for my next set, really liked that suggestion.

For the MacroFactor Nutrition, I appreciate the AI function of being able to take a picture of what I am about to eat, log it in, and later being able to look back at where I need to improve and what am I missing in my diet.

OVERALL: 

Anyone who is really interested and focused on being better without having to do a lot of extra thinking, these apps are for you. Highly suggest this to anyone who wants to level up their game.

title: Best Workout Tracker, Period!
body:
As someone who has been working out for almost a decade, I’ve tried many apps to log my workouts, track my progress, and do it all in convenience.

None have come even remotely close to this app. Being able to set multiple programs, multiple gyms with equipment availability and base your workouts on them, have them provide you a coached program or make your own, and the general great customer service are all reasons why this app is the number 1 workout tracker app out there, in my opinion.

The team is amazing at taking in feedback and releasing improvements, at no additional cost!

And their use of AI in their features actually makes sense. It’s not shoved into areas in a way that feels forced, but actually provides a benefit if you wish to use it. 

As someone in the tech field, this app is so well made that it makes me want to work at the MacroFactor team 😂 I’m very grateful that this finally entered the market.

I can honestly say that the MacroFactor Food & Workout bundle was one of the best application purchases I’ve ever made in my life, and I don’t regret it one bit.

Keep it up team!!!

title: They could make this better if they wanted
body:
This app is tremendously frustrating to use and to review. While it has a vast set of capabilities that would place it firmly at the top of anyone’ top list of workout planners and loggers but with almost every key feature comes a MASSIVE what were/are they thinking? From offering flexibility to import custom programs and adding custom exercises to progressive smart analysis, the app could be great. They then take each of these and make them frustratingly useless by either creating absurd guardrails to program import formats, making on-the-fly exercise additions something that takes longer than an entire workout to set up! If they wanted to make their app 1000x more friendly overnight they would give users a CSV template for program building and a live list of every current exercise available in the app. A junior coder could implement this feature in 10 minutes giving users so much more control over the app, but it appears MacroFactor is more interested in creating obstacles at every turn, limiting seamless program uploads to partner public figures who sell their programs for $40+. That brings me to the built-in programs that are not third-party or uploaded from a purchased source. Frankly, they are all pretty lousy and lack the detailed specificity cycle training associated with more sophisticated Trainer programs. Focus settings are nice but completely ambiguous on implementation and arbitrarily capped at various levels depending on muscle type. Creating new exercises is like solving a cypher with the number of questions to set up the exercise with non-intuitive labels and no “helper” buttons to provide a simple explanation for what the various criteria even mean. I shouldn’t have to exist the interface and have ChatGPT explain to me how MFWO classifies the “stability” of an exercise. 

Apple Health integration is another horribly executed and inconsistent feature. The app will run a custom workout simultaneously on the phone and Apple Watch but at workout conclusion it may or may not log the exercise calories in Active Calories, even when given full write privileges in Apple Health. It might just show up in Workouts. You just don’t know!

So, on potential and interface the app would score a 4.5 and on an implementation/execution perspective it deserves 0.5-1.0, but the real problem is I truly believe they have the ability to make a more capable and usable product that JUST WORKS but have chosen not to invest the time or resources into doing so. 

This is a fragmented app space and no one does it great all-around, but this app’s high ratings are truly puzzling to me! Sorry!

title: Good for brand new beginners - not much else
body: MacroFactor is the best nutrition tracking app I’ve used, and I’ve tried most of them. The workout programming feature, however, feels like a separate product built for a different user. The exercise recommendations seem to be generated for a general population with no training history or specific goals, and if you’re an intermediate lifter with a structured program already, the sessions will feel generic and somewhat random in their emphasis. For example lateral raises appeared in nearly every session of my generated split (and I did request an emphasis on those muscles) while movements more relevant to my goals were underrepresented. The app recommends a full body program which goes against most of the science backed research today. If you have a workout already building that as a custom program is incredibly time consuming and if you’re looking to migrate from spreadsheets it’s not worth it. My recommendation is use MacroFactor exclusively for nutrition tracking and run your own programming independently.

title: Useful for many but not for me
body:
So I think the main thing holding the app back is that there's almost too much fidelity in its features and exercises. It’s really nice to specify the range of motion and all the different muscle groups involved, even down to the movement plane. However, the exercise library, while fully stocked, feels overwhelming due to the sheer number of variations. 

For example, it's not just a row; it’s a chest-supported pronated grip row or a chest-supported neutral grip row. These are simple examples, but there are many more tiny nuances between exercises. Nine times out of ten, when I'm putting together a program, I just want to know where the flat bench press is, not the dozens of other variations.

The gym profiles idea seems neat at first, but it ultimately complicates things because there are so many choices of equipment, and none of them perfectly match the exercises you may have planned. If you’re in a home gym with limited equipment, you might find that the exercise you’re searching for doesn’t appear because of a small hiccup, like typing "plate loaded pull down" when the exercise is actually a "pen loaded plate down." It’s unclear why these details are so significant. The gym profiles feature becomes a hindrance with far too many exercises to choose from, creating noise when trying to assemble a program.

Once you have a program together and you’re doing the exercises, it feels pretty good at that point, but I do think the app is showing its age. Flutter, the framework it’s built on, allows for cross-platform development, which is why it looks like an Android app rather than an iOS app. This can be irritating, especially when there are free or native apps that offer similar functionality with live activities.

Another issue is that while they have access to so much data and nuance in exercises, not all of that gets exposed through the export function. When you export your data, you receive a limited set of information. While the export does contain some valuable data, it could be much more extensive for those looking to perform their own data analysis.

In summary, I think Macrofactor's workouts app is good, and I’ve used it for a long time, but it has become incredibly fussy to navigate. I wish they would adopt the same perspective they did with Macrofactor, which focuses on quick food entry. The workouts app, particularly in terms of program creation, doesn’t feel quick or efficient; it feels error-prone.

title: Great nutrition app, unacceptable workout app support
body:
Ive used MacroFactor for years, and the nutrition app is excellent. That’s the only reason I’m still a customer.

The workout side has been a completely different experience. For more than a month, core functionality was broken for me. I couldn’t reliably save changes, save warm-up routines, or create a new program. I sent screen recordings, reinstalled the app, confirmed the issue persisted, followed up repeatedly, and even asked whether there was anything else I could provide to help them reproduce it.

The response was essentially the same every time: the ticket is with the developers and there is no update.

No workaround. No meaningful status update. No timeline. No proactive communication. No request for additional logs or information. No attempt to set expectations beyond saying bugs can take weeks or months.

What bothered me most was the support experience. I was eventually told that continuing to ask for updates would not speed up the developers or otherwise help my desired resolution. That completely misses the point of customer support. I was not asking support to write the code. I was asking for some level of ownership, communication, and help while a paid product was nearly unusable.

If a company knows a serious issue may take weeks or months to resolve, I would expect some proactive effort to retain and satisfy the affected customer. Instead, compensation or extended access was only mentioned after I became increasingly frustrated and raised the issue myself.

I ultimately gave up, cancelled the workout portion, and moved my training to another app.

The nutrition app is still good enough that I continue to use it, which says a lot about how strong that product is. But the workout app and the way this issue was handled have seriously damaged my confidence in MacroFactor as a whole.

If you are considering the workout app specifically, understand that if you hit a serious bug, you may be waiting a very long time with little more than “the developers have your ticket.”
Where has this app been all my life? lol

title: IT DOES THE WORK!
body:
I’ve really been enjoying MacroFactor Workouts. The workout builder is clean, easy to use, and makes tracking my training simple. It’s become a big part of my routine.

The only downside is that it can be a bit buggy at times. Every now and then things don’t sync correctly or the app feels a little unstable, but nothing that completely ruins the experience.

One feature I’d love to see is an Apple Watch app. Being able to start workouts, log sets, rest timers, and track everything directly from my watch would make the experience even better and much more convenient in the gym.

Overall, it’s a great workout app with a lot of potential. Fixing the occasional bugs and adding Apple Watch support would easily make it one of the best fitness apps available.

I’ll be a subscriber for as long as this app exists. Highly recommend.

title: Lots of current issues, all fixable
body:
The bad: Generally over engineered, unintuitive. Lacks video examples of women performing exercises. Buggy: have lost multiple workout sessions due to workouts getting stuck and unable to complete. Way too many clicks to just see what I did on an exercise last session. Doesn’t tell me the name of the workout in the history logs. Can’t see actual set logs from dashboard. Appears to use some weird rolling window algo to calculate 1rm instead of discrete logged sets so that even when I lift less with the same weight my 1rm goes up for that session. Doesn’t allow you to change your logged set’s weight or reps without resetting rest timer. Exercise naming conventions are precise but hard to recognize on dash board when cutoff: half my exercises just say “Plate-Loaded…” or “Overhand Grip Pin Loaded…” and never get to the only thing I want to see there which is “Shoulder Press” or “Machine Row”. Can’t search for exercises to add to dashboard, must scroll through everything. Impossible to add two of the same exact workout to a single cycle without duplicating it, resulting in duplicating work when adding/removing exercises from that workout. The time estimates for a workout are wildly inaccurate, completely underselling how long a given workout will take. To make a point I plugged in Jeff’s own “45 minute leg routine” and the app guessed it would take 14 minutes. 

The good: sleek ui. Easily swap exercises during a session. Easy to add/remove sets or exercises during a session. Extremely wide and precise available exercise selection. Easily see number of sets per muscle per week

body: I started using the MacroFactor (food tracking) app at the beginning of this year when I decided to embark on my first honest-to-God cut in 5 years and I instantly fell in love. Fast forward a few months and I decided to get the MacroFactor Workouts app and being impressed continued! This app is phenomenal! Tracking your workouts, seemingly unlimited machine and setup variations, and so much more. I love the ability to upload/import other programs you have excel/Google Sheets for, the exercise/equipment swap feature, and so much more make this such an amazing app. There are a few changes I’d love to see, but none are enough to hurt the 5-Star review! Highly recommend this app for workout and training tracking/progress. Be prepared to have to edit some of the weights and ranges that are prescribed in your first few weeks but once it learns your strength, etc. Additionally, I HIGHLY recommend coupling this with the nutrition tracking MacroFactor app because the combined price is unbeatable! Highly recommend both across the board!

Also would be great if we had an option if we want to prioritize certain heavy lifts. Would also be cool if the ai coach could identify muscle imbalances and can suggest to the user if we want to focus on our imbalances.

title: Like it, needs work
body:
I was very excited for this app, but it doesn’t integrate other programs the Jeff Nippard offers. Any time I try to set up a suggested program, it offers only full body or UL. That has me disappointed as I was very hopeful there would be more options. Also some exercises I use frequently or want to use as a substitute do have the video demo. 

I do run my own program and like the features it has from sessions to session, such as the suggested weight and reps. I will continue to use this since it’s included with the MacroFactor subscription, but I am hopeful some improvements can be made.  I do believe this app has promise.

title: An app for serious gym goers
body:
While it requires spending some time setting it up, once you’ve configured a program that you like it’s so easy to just show up in the gym and hit play.

The way that notes stick makes it easy to remember and add things that I read on Reddit or TikTok with regard to form.

And the super fast swap mechanism makes it easy to keep sessions short even during busy gym time.

I’ve tried all the other apps and this one is by far the best. Thanks for making it, team. It’s clearly made by people who get it.

title: Neat and flexible
body: I like how it’s easy to swap exercises, dose the math for you when switching between units and machines, plus the simple design of the interface

title: Bad
body: Nearly unusable as is. First, it created a workout plan with an absurd amount of volume. Second, the smart progression feature is useless. After painstakingly editing all the weight counts for every machine and weight set it still recommends stupid amounts of reps per exercise OUTSIDE of the rep goal window it recommends! Or weight that isn’t within the weight parameters I set. So I had to disable. All said and done what I ended up with after all the editing and feature disabling was just a workout tracker app like Strong but with a far more complicated UI. Not worth it. Really disappointed. I hope this reaches a developer as I have been a long time Jeff Nippard fan and a daily religious macro factor user.

title: Best I’ve ever tried
body: This has all the features I’ve looked for for years including a workout timer and sooooo much other grate features

title: Game changer!
body: I’ve followed Jeff Nippard on YouTube for awhile and I’m super happy he finally released a science-based workout app. The app is awesome and I’ve seen noticeable improvement. Plus it’s just cool to see all the progress in the app! It’s the best combo of workouts and workout tracking!!

title: Great companion to Macrofactor diet app
body: A great companion to Macrofactor diet. Easy to use, quick to add workouts and good customization. What I like most is that it scales well to training level, where a new trainee has resources like video tutorials and an advanced trainee has access to RPE info. Been training for ~9 years and it’s better than pen and paper and phone notepad in a low-interference way that I like

title: I want to like this but it needs work!!
body:
While I like a lot about the app, there is more that I don’t like that has me hesitant to switch. Here are the issues I keep running into:
1) when I try to create a custom exercise I almost always get a message saying “this used to be a custom exercise, but it is no longer on our radar.”  So it will not let me add any data or use it as an exercise. 
2) the naming of exercises is all over the place. 
3) the suggestions for weight and reps often don’t make sense. They will reduce weight it reps even if I was within the set rep goal on the previous workout day or even the previous set. 
4) this is small but there is nothing that tells you that you just set a PR. It’s nice and can be motivating to see that when it happens. 
5) when searching for an exercise and trying to filter them by a specific muscle, it will show you every exercise that has that muscle listed even if it’s listed as a secondary muscle. So when I search for a rear Delt exercise I get just about every back exercise. This makes the filter about worthless. 

There are some other minor issues but these are the main ones that keep me from using this as my main app.

title: Almost perfect!
body:
Switched from Strong after 5 years.
The rep expectations are spot on and the program generation is super easy. I also love how easy it is to switch exercises when traveling and hotel gyms don’t have my home gym equipment.

My only request is that it have an Apple Watch app to make it easy to check reps/weights before a set and mark a set as done.

title: Incredible
body: I’ve used several fitness trackers and workout generators and this blows them out of the water. Combine the fact you can upload Jeff Nippard programs seamlessly and this creates the perfect system.

title: Everything you need
body: This app is very in depth. It takes a little while to set up and get comfortable with, but it’s worth it. The programming is quite good and the specificity for equipment is top notch.

title: Lack of integrations
body: I would probably rate it a 5 star if I was able to actually import workouts and track other things like running

title: Couple suggestions
body: Long-time customer of MacroFactor, really want to like the Workouts app but find it’s not sticking with me yet. Don’t like that I can’t easily modify a routine once I start it, and also wish the weekly workouts mixed up exercises while still targeting same muscles for consistency. The same exact routine week to week is too boring, for me at least.

title: Rings
body: It’s an amazing app, but it messes with your workout and Move ring on your Apple Watch, and it will subtract the workout when you hit complete in the app.

title: Great!
body: I like everything about this app. I’ve been weight lifting for about 6 years, and I’m a little older. For me, the auto progression combined with RIR is perfect. I will say it took me a few workouts to learn the lay of the land, but pretty easy for the most part and I think is to be expected. I have also used most of the weight training apps in the App Store for comparison.

title: Terrible!
body: Absolutely hate this app. It is entirely non-intuitive, the workout duration is not accurate, you cannot change the program after you’ve set up the app, and the recommended reps and sets are awful. I can’t believe how disappointed I am in this app.

title: Gets worse the more you use it
body: I really liked this program the first week I did it. Now, the suggested workouts are a waste of time. Somehow week over week I’m doing less and less and the workouts aren’t progressing. Sometimes it gives me impossible sets like overhead barbell press at 1lb. The weight progression it recommends often means taking off one weight to rack 6 more so you go down by 2.5 or small increments. I may try using it to track my own lifts but the AI usage here sucks. It’s true of MacroFactor as well where it’s recommended I stay on a 1400 calorie diet for over a year.

title: Great idea could be better
body: I like the app my only gripe is that there is no cardio in my program and I can’t figure how to get in

title: Best workout app I’ve ever seen!
body: Makes tracking and keeping up with progress effortless.

title: Needs Apple Watch support
body: This really needs Apple Watch support. It’s crazy in 2026 fitness apps don’t support the watch. It’s a really great app but this is a real downer for me.

title: Macro factor Workout Tracker
body: Awesome App with very detailed instructions and how-to videos filmed from 3 viewpoints.  Is far better than hiring a personal trainer.

title: The perfect workout app
body:
Finally an app
That enables easy workout generation and tracking !

title: Best workout app I’ve used
body: Tracks almost anything a serious lifter could want. Great videos and info on each exercise. Smart substitutions. And if you’ve ever bought Jeff Nippard’s programs in the past, they plug seamlessly into the app. I’m using the Bodybuilding Transformation System and loving it!

title: No recommended weights for sets and reps
body: Doesn’t suggest weights for the workouts so it can learn or so you can get started overcomplicated to use , Fitbod is less complicated and easier to use.

title: From tedious to manageable
body: Tracking my progression and aligning it with a strategy has always been tedious and cumbersome for me, and I’ve tried many methods, but so far, MacroFactor’s approach has been my favorite. Excited to see how the app evolves with my progress.

title: Good App
body: Good app but pretty expensive for what it is, I get a free membership with my Macrofactor subscription.

title: App sucks
body: MF app is awesome. MF workouts app is such a disappointment. Very bland compared to many other free apps. I have a full gym with most equipment and machines. But the app gives me the same exercises over and over, every week. The only positive thing i can say about the app is the UI. Besides that, very meh. Any AI out there can create a better workout programs for you. Don’t waste your money.

title: After searching for forever, finally found a solution
body: Great app, allows me to do everything I can in an excel spreadsheet. Super customizable, letting me plan out an entire mesocycle with ease. I would like to see improvement in the data though. For example, show me a log of my workout lengths

title: Best Workout Friend!
body: Just completed my first six week program and I am eager to start the next one! This is the first time in my life that I’ve worked out consistently for 6 in a row because this app made it very easy to integrate into my daily routine. The app makes it easy to swap one particular upper body/arm exercise for another on days that my injured shoulder is experiencing increased inflammation.

title: Changed my health and my life
body: This app changed how I approached my training and how I treat my body. Not only can I add my physical therapy movements in here but I can also train to meet my strength goals. All in all, this app kind of changed my life and has only improved my quality of life. Thank you Jeff and the MacroFactor team! I appreciate you creating an app that will hopefully keep changing dozens of people's lives.

title: Great app - Still early
body: Amazing app (I’ve been using MacroFactor a long time and this is just as good). Love the auto progression and RiR system. It is missing a few things I’d consider essential though - namely Apple Watch tracking (or any Apple watch version at all) and a live activity on iOS to show workout progress.

title: Pros and cons. Net con.
body: The muscles targeted diagram is helpful to see where you’ve neglected. But the rep ranges, weight amount, and reps in reserve all fluctuate so much set to set and day to day that it’s nearly impossible to determine and track progressive overload. If that’s a metric the app considers and manages for you, that is not clear at all. I’ll be returning to Strong.

title: Tucker Cera
body: Keeps me on track and give me a good plan

title: Insane value. MAKE sure to coach yourself too!
body:
I had been using MacroFactor, the nutrition app, on and off for about a year and was excitedly waiting for the workouts app to come out to have cohesion with the data and user flow. 

The app is a dream and such a natural extension of the regular MacroFactor app, which has been receiving a lot of support and updates over the time I've been using it as well. There are waay more things to like and love than dislike about both of these apps. 

One thing to keep in mind while doing the workouts is to *stay present in your body* and be aware of when you're starting to feel:
1. Any pain
2. Lower range of motion
3. Tingling or other sensations in your muscles

It can be easy to push yourself with this app since it wants to help you get stronger and stronger, and it often puts higher and higher weight loads on you in ways that can seem pretty fast for me at times. 

YOU are your ground truth, not stats and plans in an app.

title: Really like the app but has a glitch
body:
So far I’m really enjoying this app. It’s intuitive and the UI is so easy to use. I love how I can customize my home gym so it knows what workouts I’m able to do. 
My one complaint is there seems to be a glitch where if you’re sharing your health app info with it and use the apple fitness app at the same time as this app to track your calories then your active calories will not be counted towards your move ring. It’s a minor inconvenience but if this was fixed then I’d give this app 5 stars easy.

title: Beta test
body: JN is really cool like his stuff stoked at trying new app! Currently on the fence if I should leave another app and join this one so far so good!

title: One of the best lifting apps!
body:
My original review had some features at launch that weren’t there. The MF team doesn’t disappoint in regard to continuously adding features. Im coming from using “strong” for ~4+ years — and I can confidently say MF Workouts is one of the best apps there is for lifting. 🔥

1. More splits — PPL, 5-day ULPPL, etc. *** UPDATE: MF team has confirmed PPL & UL-PPL 😊
2. Cardio? *** UPDATE: they added basic cardio functions!! 
3. Would like this to track in apple health for a workout. *** UPDATE: done!

title: Lets me focus on just doing the workout
body:
Great app, takes a lot of the thinking out of both the planning and the workout itself and the demos and explanations are fantastic.

A couple issues I’d love to see addressed:
 - Many exercises call for band assistance but the way bands are quantified in the app isn’t helpful. It will call for an exact weight but my bands have a range. I wish I could input the bands I have with their ranges and colors and have the app work with that rather than suggest -125.5 and force me to correct it every time. Also I don’t think these band ratings are even that accurate so the suggested reps are always way off. Perhaps focus on progression rather than exact weight for bands?
 - Very minor but I have 8 and 12 lb dumbbells but I can only specify 7.5 and 12.5

title: Buggy app
body: App keeps crashing and workouts cannot get activated.

title: It’s alright, definitely better out there though.
body:
After using MacroFactor  for a year or so, I was excited to learn that Jeff Nippard came out with a new app similar to it but for working out. However, after using it for a few weeks, it is fairly lack luster compared to other training apps out there such as “the train app.” So here’s the pros and cons.

The pros:

The app is definitely nice. It used the same formula as the macro factor app to make workouts for you. This is extremely nice especially when you want to gain strength. Specifically, I think the best feature of this app is its ability to help you find the correct weight for each set. So far in my workouts, the app is mostly spot on. If I’m doing leg curls and the app recommends 11 reps at x weight… 11 reps is nearly perfect every-time. Along with this the feature that is has for each rep range, such as failure or 2 reps in reserve, is very convenient and really helps you stay on track each workout. The next biggest pro is that the app has, I think, EVERY possible exercise there is at any gym. 

The cons: 

While the pros of this app are definitely big time pros the cons make it hard to really say the app is worth it compared to other training apps. For one, the alert for when it’s time for your set is not great. Yes it will give you a little bell but other apps I’ve used will give you multiple alerts. For example, if I’m doing a set and the rest time is 1:30 at 30 seconds I’ll get an alert in my AirPods saying “30 seconds” repeat at 15 seconds and then a count down at 5 and it automatically turns up the music. The workouts app does not do this and only gives a small bell as an indicator to a set. Next, other apps will actually connect to your Apple Watch. A big plus to this is that they also track the reps you do (if it’s an upper body exercise or a squat like exercise of course). Sadly the workouts app does not, in my opinion this really helps in the gym as you do ever have to count reps and can just focus on the exercise and mind muscle connection itself. The last con I have is actually just some of the exercises that are suggested themselves. While I’m sure they must be the greatest exercises scientifically for muscle growth. Some of these exercises suggested do feel like a waste of time. Nordic hamstring curls are great for a high school football team that may not have a big enough weight room for everyone to get reps in. However, Nordic hamstring curls are not good if you’re at a gym and have multiple machines to hit hamstrings and glutes.  

With all this said, I would recommend this app to anyone who has used MacroFactor in the past or if you’re new to the gym. However if you’re experienced in the gym,  there are other apps that are just better.

title: Love the smart progression
body: I’ve tried a bunch of different workout apps (including some from those who are generally respected in the fitness space). This one beats them all in my opinion. The progression is realistic and I’m surprised at how spot on it is most of the time. It’s easy to log and I love that it’s seamless with the MacroFactor app (which I also love). I like the customizability and they’ve got good reports too. If you’re waffling on whether or not to try it, I think it’s a no-brainer. And if you do food logging anyway, the bundle price is a steal when looking at similar app combos (workout + food logging).

I’m just getting back into working out after 3 years off and with limited equipment available to me I find this app extremely easy because you can select the things you have available and it gives you workouts that you can do with that. Also the exercise selection is very good and intuitive to swap out for anything else that can also hit the muscles you want. Love it!

title: Happy so far
body: Happy in general so far. I think the explanations are too verbose tho. Maybe have the high level overview of the exercise and then allow the user to tap a chevron to find more info on a particular section. Im trying to filter out most of the info a lot of times. For example the eccentric calf raise gave several different examples of what to use for a step. Seems unnecessary

title: Overall fine
body: Decent workout app but listed exercises for certain workouts aren’t too appealing like doing two tibialis anterior excesses in one workout while other groups are only hit once. Or doing two lower back extension exercises in one workout. Sometimes rep ranges seem nonsensical where it averages 11-13 ranges but then some exercises give a random 30 to 40 reps out of no where

title: Very good
body: It is a very well made app but it is not designed for an athlete at all.

title: Falls Short of Competition
body:
I have used several workout apps this one falls short of the competition.  No Apple Watch integration - means I have to carry my phone around in the gym. Also means heart rate is not tracked so Apple Health data is incomplete.

Also cannot import workout/exercise history from other apps.  Not an issue for beginners. But those of us with tons of lifting behind us don’t want to start over on our progress or PRs.  

I also certainly do not need confetti cannons going off every time I complete a set.  These little celebrations are a distraction and aren’t helping anyone lift.

title: Making gains!
body: Love the dynamic reps and RIR. I’m making more progress in the past few weeks of using the app than I have in the past few months following a basic program using a different app. Knowing it’s fairly new I’m sure they’ll make more improvements, but top of mind is having an exercise match the program setup and variability if it was added manually. Nice work overall!

title: Amazing app — language is the only barrier
body:
Excellent app — the best for workouts and progress tracking. The features are very complete and really help you stay consistent and see results.
However, as a Brazilian, I struggle a lot with the language. There’s no option for Brazilian Portuguese (PT-BR). If you add PT-BR, this app will be absolutely perfect and will definitely reach many more people.

title: Really disappointed
body:
This is my first ever app review, and leaving it because I’m a huge fan of Jeff’s and love his MacroFactor Nutrition app, but the Workouts app is not doing it for me. 

Positives:
* Gives suggested weights/reps to progress
* Is integrated with the MacroFactor Nutrition app

Negatives:
* No audio on rest timer (even with the “play sound” setting toggled on)
* If I log a set and it’s incorrect, and I don’t notice it til halfway through my rest, once I edit it, it starts my rest timer over from the beginning
* Also, if I log a set and it’s incorrect and I need to adjust it, as soon as I tap it to make the changes, it removes what I already put in and resets it to what the suggest weight and reps were, which is annoying if I only needed to make one quick little change
* There have been times I go to do an exercise, and it shows my previous workout having used much more weight than I did. Realized I missed the decimal when logging it last time, and there’s no way to edit my weight/reps from previous workouts, so it’s throwing off my data
* It can be difficult/annoying trying to find specific exercises- have to scroll FOREVER through the extensive list of exercises to find what I’m looking for. Even difficult when searching because the exercise I’m looking for is in a very specific name
* Also trying to swap a given exercise with one I’d already manually added in before, but when I search for it, it doesn’t appear. Exercises are just difficult to find in general. 
* Some weight/rep recommendations are awful: my last workout with doing pull ups, my max reps were 10, now it want me to target the 16-18 rep range?!? This is really disappointing because this is the biggest feature I was looking forward to to help me with progressive overload
* I’ve had issues where the rest timer didn’t start automatically after logging a set, so I went to start it myself, but then saw the rest timer wasn’t even there for some reason
* I can understand not having video demonstrations for exercises I added manually, there are exercises, that I’d never heard of/seen, that are given to me by the built-in, provided program, not having video demonstrations (the dumbbell frog pump for example)

Overall, very annoyed and disappointed with the app. I enjoyed logging my workouts with the Strong app MUCH more.

title: Add watch features please
body: I would love to have the ability to track stuff on my watch while I workout kind of like the app heavy

title: Amazing
body:
I’ve been lifting around 5-6 times a week for more than 20 years. For breaking up monotony and busting plateaus - this app has been excellent. I’m dropping the multi-decade bro-split and trying new exercises without the need to overthink and plan before every workout.

The ability to craft supersets/circuits as well swapping in alts is top notch. 

It’s an incredibly well designed app. Can’t imagine how nice this would be for new lifters.

title: Loving it so far!
body:
This is an amazing app. Loving it so far. 

Would like if the timer made a noise even if my phone was on silent and or in focus mode. I have the setting enabled for it to bypass DnD. 

I would also like to have it round to the nearest 5lb or similar. I can’t do 47 pounds on a pin loaded machine for example. 

Lastly, I would like to be able to set the default rep range and or for it to not do odd number reps. Not sure why it keeps doing 9-11 reps or 5-7 instead of 8-12 / 6-8. Doesn’t 8-12 make more sense? 

I’ll keep providing feedback as I continue to use it.

Thank you!

title: Best workout app with room to improve
body:
I’ve given the app 5 stars because it really does stand out especially on release. Fully featured in terms of exercise selection, building out a program, connecting with macrofactor etc. 

Gym profiles makes it so easy for me to select different gyms like Planet fitness, Work, and Home. Makes it super easy for me to get my workouts in.

I don’t know if this was by “happenstance” but I started a very aggressive cut in MacroFactor. The workout app program reps and sets decreased quite a bit I noticed and my weight load increased a bit. HUGE help and made my life easier but again I do not know if this was a freak deload or what. Super useful and convenient timing for the start of my cut.

That being said there is room to improve. I’d like to see recommendations for cardio. I saw equipment get added but I think all programs should get optional cardio available to add as it would be nice to account for. 

Another glaring problem which is being worked on I’m sure is program options. Bro splits and PPL missing was a huge surprise. You can always import or make workouts but it is odd to be missing on launch. 

Noticed some equipment has pictures but no videos but I’m sure the team is actively working on that. 

Overall great app and look forward to coming updates.

title: Great app but…
body: It needs better cardio integration. Cardio is arguably one of, if not the most important aspect of working out but there’s no option to add cardio into a workout plan. Thus you never actually get the opportunity to do cardio using the app. At that point, why should anyone even use this app?

title: By far the best
body: I’ve been loving the program I’m on for the past three weeks with this app after lifting for years both on my own and with a coach. Having already had MacroFactor I just jumped right into this app and I’m never looking back. I can feel myself getting better already. It’s helped me break out of a training rut I’ve been in and helped me see the value of the equipment my gym has in a new light.

title: Download this now
body: I never write reviews because i’m lazy but this app rocks. 100% worth the subscription. I like it well enough to take a break after my workout to write this because it actually really is that good.

title: Needs Worl
body: App has a lot of potential but sometimes they make your workout certain areas to much. For example the app set up for me to do 4 separate chest exercises in 5 days. How does it not expect me to be sore.

title: Game changer for a beginner
body: Helps my ADHD, gives me all the guidance I need to keep up with my workouts.

title: Honestly great app
body:
I never really review apps, but this one is so well done I felt the need to write a review. 

2 things I don’t like/need a fix: it should be easier to switch gym profiles. When I change the gym I’m working out it won’t change my suggested workouts for the week, so I had to delete the two other gyms I go to because it was bothering me. Second thing is sometimes it suggests weights I don’t have or aren’t available on the pin machines. I put in my ez bar weights (which are jump by tens) sometimes it suggests weights like 35 lbs 

Besides that amazing app

title: Fantastic app
body: Really loving this app! Already use the calorie tracker and this pair together perfectly!!

title: Best workout app on the market
body: This app is only going to get better, between Jeff’s expertise and the team developing this app I can’t honestly complain about anything without coming off like a nitpick-y Karen. Thank you for developing this app!!

title: Strong Start
body: Takes all the mystery out of programming and progression, has a huge library of exercises, customizable gyms and a beautiful interface. They came out the gate strong with this one. I look forward to the updates as they make their way down the roadmap.

title: Mediocre
body:
This app generates very subpar workouts. I was expecting for the app to actually have training templates created by real coaches. 

It’s hard to find exercises since there’s so many with the same name. The UI is very cluttered.

title: Promising
body: Pretty intuitive until you get to an exercise that doesn’t have a video/photo, or swaps for things that aren’t in your gym. It’s obviously new and I’m sure it will only get better.

title: Awesome app, some tweaks to make it perfect
body:
1. I turned off rest timers in settings, yet they still go off and notify my phone when it ends. I have double checked settings in each workout and rest timers are off. Please fix
2. Workout videos are great, I’d suggest shortening the first video to the workout movement, and erase the walking into frame. Keep the long video there but as a 2nd or 3rd option like you already have for the secondary angles.

title: Woah!
body:
Literally the workout app I’ve been waiting for! Ease of use. Clear instructions. Step by step video guides & a full blown FAQ. What more could you want? I love that I can import my Nippard workouts into the app. Hopefully the full library will soon be made importable once you’ve purchased. 

Can’t wait to see how this app grows in the future!

title: Easy to Use! #brotivated
body: Love this app. Just started using it and it makes tracking workout so easy. I look forward to each workout half because I want to keep up tracking!

title: Hard Truth
body: Since no one wants to say it, I will. The app UI/UX is trash. If you are a beginner and just need the app to pop out a workout split and can’t manually figure out progressive overload I could see this being beneficial. The easiest way to build a split is to either get stuck with a full body or push pull split that isn’t exactly what you want or to pay Jeff for a plan that you could upload to the app with ease. If you want to build from scratch you will be stuck spending over an hour doing so. Finding the specific exercises you want in this interface is abysmal, the screen is too busy, many exercises don’t have a video along side it. Ultimately I’ve given up because this app should have stayed in beta. I’ll come check it out maybe in 6 months to see if things have changed. One more thing, the name sucks. “MacroFactor Workouts” makes no sense. MacroFactor makes sense for the standalone app but calling a Workout app Macro anything is not smart.

title: Great, not perfect
body:
I’ve used more than a dozen hypertrophy, strength and mobility training apps from all the big personalities and companies in this space.  The MF Workouts app is very very good.  Two things hold it back.  

One:  I can’t add/track cardio and or mobility work easily.  This is, by far, the single biggest flaw in almost all of these apps. They all track one thing very well, but none of them track an entire fitness regimen end to end.  There are some apps that will do this, but they’re so clunky that a 45 to 60 minute workout takes an extra 10 to 15 minutes because the in-app workflow is horrible.   

Two: Poor Apple Health integration.  Right now you have to track your workout on your watch separately to log heart rate, workout length, caloric burn, etc. I think it’s on their roadmap but they don’t earn five stars until this is done.

title: Overly complicated-Too rigid
body:
This app had promise, but it collapses under its own complexity. Instead of enabling training, it actively gets in the way. Basic workout creation is unnecessarily constrained, forcing users into the app’s logic rather than supporting how experienced lifters actually train.

I paid for a tool and got a maze. The hype leans heavily on “science” and optimization, but that clearly didn’t trickle down to the actual user experience. What’s presented as intelligent design feels more like rigid dogma wrapped in marketing.

For anyone who already understands programming and progression, this is not just disappointing, it’s unusable. I’m cancelling and returning to something simpler, faster, and actually intuitive.

title: Opinion
body: Overall really well gave it a 5 stars because the app is very well managed and easy to understand, you can also adjust the workout based on the equipment you have , there is a variety of different workouts and after a month I have noticed a bigger difference. My favorites  part is the body diagram where it shows which muscles you workout the most and it breaks down how many sets you did for that and you can prioritize different muscle groups and it also syncs really well with the MacroFactor app.

title: BS Squat Video please
body:
Hey Jeff and team,
Great job on this app. Looking forward to more video exercises. I do Dumbbell Bulgarian split squats. I’d like to see you add a video with them and this could be a feature where you have two versions 1. With more knee flexion for quads and 2. With lead foot further out for glutes. Also I think you should rename it to Bulgarian Split Squat (more recognizable) over its current name in the app “Elevated rear leg split squats”.
